title: Explore the gender pay gap and test your knowledge

breadcrumb.text: Explore the gender pay gap and test your knowledge

body.text: 26 October 2017
The gender pay gap for full-time employees now stands at 9.1% in favour of men, the lowest since records began in 1997.

body.box_text:
What is the gender pay gap?

Calculated as the difference between average hourly earnings (excluding overtime) of men and women as a proportion of average hourly earnings (excluding overtime) of men’s earnings. It is the primary measure used when comparing differences in pay between men and women.

[](#interactive)

body.text: The UK government has committed to closing the gender pay gap and introduced new legislation requiring all companies with 250 or more employees to disclose their pay gap [in a register](https://genderpaygap.campaign.gov.uk/) by April 2018.

One of the widest gender pay gaps is in financial occupations. ONS data show, for example, that female financial institution managers and directors earn 26.2% less, on average, than men in the same occupation. The pay gap varies considerably across occupations, and in some cases there is no difference in earnings between men and women, or women earn more than men.
Can you guess which occupations see the largest difference in earnings for men and women?

body.h3: What causes the gender pay gap?
body.text: What causes the gender pay gap?

body.h3: What causes the gender pay gap?
body.text: The underlying causes of the gender pay gap are complex and may include:

body.h3: What causes the gender pay gap?
body.text: more women work in lower-paid jobs or sectors

body.h3: What causes the gender pay gap?
body.text: women are more likely to work part-time, which can mean a lower rate of pay

body.h3: What causes the gender pay gap?
body.text: women are under-represented in senior roles -this may be due to attitudes about gender roles, lack of flexible working or women taking time to look after their family
